https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-and-russia.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IVzx Russia's attack on the Ukrainian port city of Odesa damaged several buildings and vehicles Image: Nina Liashonok/REUTERS Advertisement Overnight drone and missile attacks have killed several people and injured dozens more according to various local authorities in Ukraine and Russia . In the southern Russian city of Belgorod, near the Ukrainian border, at least five people were killed and 25 injured. Belgorod's acting governor said that several apartment blocks had been hit overnight and images posted to social media showed several fires. Belgorod is a key logistics hub for Russian offensives in Kharkiv and the Donbass. Russian authorities, who said more than 150 Ukrainian drones had been downed by their forces overnight, also reported attacks on the Black Sea ports of Novorossiysk and Gelendzhik. Novorossiysk is home to key Russian oil export facilities. 'Russia continuing its war on global food security' says Zelenskyy Russian attacks targeted oil refineries in the Sumy region as well as the port city of Odesa, where President Voldymyr Zelenskyy said at least eight people had been injured. The Odesa strikes targeted oil facilities in the southern port. Odesa is also one of Ukraine's most important agricultural export hubs. Zelenskyy said that with Sunday's attack, "Russia is continuing its war on global food security." Two people were also killed and at least 21 injured in a Russian attack on Kharkiv in eastern Ukraine, according to regional head Oleh Syniehubov. Across the border, Russia claimed its forces had taken control of two villages in eastern Donetsk, though the claim could not be independently verified. Ukraine calls on allies to help with air defenses To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Kyiv arming itself against 4-year Russia invasion As Russia's war on Ukraine drags on toward the five-year mark, Kyiv is again short on defensive weapons. Kyiv has desperately sought to acquire more medium and long-range weapons systems from the US with mixed results. Now, Ukraine is turning to Turkey for help as the US reportedly depletes its own stockpiles with its still unresolved war in Iran. On Sunday, Ukraine's military news outlet Militarnyi reported that it would be purchasing 70 ATACMS and 12 M270 multiple-launch rocket systems from Turkey in an order that will also include more than 2,500 227mm rockets with cluster-munitions payloads. The US, which has 30 days to approve the sale, estimates its total value at $283 million (€245 million). The ATACMS in question are of an older design, with a range limited to 165 kilometers (102.5 miles). https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/world-news.text: Incredible footage has captured the moment three men saved the life of a toddler after she fell from a fifth-floor balcony. The incredible rescue took place on Sunday in Lomza, Poland, which is about 90 miles from the national capital of Warsaw . Emergency crews rushed to the scene after receiving reports that a small child was dangling off a balcony at a high-rise apartment block. When first responders arrived, neighbours who had already spotted the girl, who was clinging on to the side of the building for dear life, had gathered below to help. Stunning footage captured the moment three neighbours stretched out a blanket to catch the girl if she fell - which she did, moments thereafter. Łomża Police deputy commissioner Karolina Wojciekian confirmed to Polish news station Radio Bialystok that that emergency crews were called to the scene at a residential apartment building just after 2pm on Sunday. "Just after 2pm, we received a report that a child was on the fifth floor of a residential complex in Łomża, clinging to the outside of the balcony railing with her hands," she said. "Moments later, the child fell, but neighbours managed to spread a blanket on which the child had fallen. Thanks to their quick actions, tragedy was averted." Deputy Commissioner Wojciekian added that the girl, aged four, was "conscious and taken to the hospital" for further assessment by first responders when they arrived at the scene. Ultimately, the tot walked away from the horror incident with only a few minor bruises. One of the neighbours that caught the small child, Dariusz Płoński, told Radio Bialystok that he went outside to investigate what the hubbub was all about in front of the apartment building in which he lived. "When I left the building, I heard people screaming. I looked up and saw a child there, almost naked, only wearing a T-shirt. "The girl was on one side of the barrier, then the other. I shouted at her not to move, but she didn't react. Then one of the neighbours appeared with a blanket, and the three of us jumped onto the terrace below the balcony." He revealed that the incredible blanket rescue happened in the blink of an eye. "I shouted for someone to help, but the people either didn't hear me or were afraid. In any case, the three of us spread the blanket," he said. "It was seconds, because when I looked up again and saw the child was already in a different place, we barely had time to move ourselves before she fell onto the blanket." Płoński stated that the girl did bump her head after she bounced from the blanket and onto the ground, but one of the neighbours - a doctor - assessed her at the scene before paramedics arrived and determined she had some bumps, bruises, and maybe a sprained ankle. “It was a matter of seconds,” he said, adding: “When I looked up again and saw that the child had moved to another spot, we barely had time to move into position so she would fall onto the blanket.” Despite the tot being left seemingly unattended, police later confirmed that her 27-year-old mother was, in fact, home at the time of the horror incident. She was, however, asleep inside the apartment as her daughter had a near-miss with utter calamity, while the girl's father was abroad for work. Łomża Municipal Police Headquarters press officer Urszula Brulińska confirmed police are now considering charges against the mother as she was later found to be drunk. She had a blood-alcohol level of 0.07 - or 70mg alcohol per 100ml of blood - which is considered to be a moderate level of drunkenness. For context, Polish drivers cannot get behind the wheel of a car with a blood alcohol reading of more than 0.02. A police investigation is continuing, but, if the mum is charged, it would likely be for 'exposing a child to an immediate danger of death or serious bodily harm'. If convicted, the mum may face up to five years in prison.

It remains unclear who or what was behind the alleged activity Photograph: Toby Shepheard/Reuters UK news Local representatives question official accounts after suspected bomb plot at RAF Fairford Amid conflicting statements, local MP and councillors demand answers over how suspects were allowed to enter residential areas of nearby village Jamie Grierson Mon 28 Sep 2026 15.13 EDT Last modified on Mon 28 Sep 2026 18.46 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google An MP and councillors representing the residents of the village near RAF Fairford who were evacuated due to a suspected terror plot have expressed scepticism and concern over the security response to threats made by Iran. About 85 properties in Whelford, Gloucestershire, were evacuated on Sunday morning after five men were arrested on suspicion of explosives offences in the village. The men, who were later re-arrested on suspicion of terror offences, were released on bail on Monday. It is understood some residents were returning to their properties late on Monday, but a cordon remains around the village. As speculation mounted over the circumstances surrounding the incident, concerns emerged about how events were handled by the authorities. In July, Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps noted RAF Fairford’s use by US bombers, warning the UK that “any base used for aggression against Iranian territory constitutes a legitimate target for our forces”. However, it remains unclear who or what was behind the alleged activity. Iran has denied any involvement. Tehran’s embassy in London condemned what it described as “unfounded and malicious speculation” linking the country to the incident in the vicinity of the military base in Gloucestershire. Roz Savage, the MP for South Cotswolds, said she had many questions about the circumstances of how the alleged terror plot was averted. View image in fullscreen US air force personnel work on a B1 bomber at RAF Fairford on Monday. Photograph: Alastair Grant/AP The Liberal Democrat MP, whose constituency covers the military base, said she would be writing to the prime minister and the defence secretary with her concerns. “Ever since it was first announced six months ago that RAF Fairford was going to be used as the base for US military airstrikes on Iran, I’ve been asking questions of the government about whether they can assure my residents, my constituents, of their safety,” she said. “They had given that assurance. However, I feel that the events of this weekend do cast that into doubt.” She went on: “Who knew what? When did they know it? Where was the ball dropped? What more could have been done to secure the safety and security of my constituents? “We are already in the process of writing to the secretary of state for defence and to the prime minister to try and ascertain the answers to some of these questions.” There have been conflicting statements about who knew what and when. A farmer from Whelford told reporters she called police in the early hours of Sunday to report suspicious activity – which then triggered a rapid response. But the US president, Donald Trump, also suggested to reporters the men had been under surveillance. Now, the men have been released on police bail. Tristan Wilkinson, a cabinet member for Cotswold district council and councillor for the Lechlade, Kempsford and Fairford South ward, which covers Whelford, said: “The American president indicated last night in front of journalists that there was some intelligence and that these individuals were under surveillance. “If that was to be true, that they would have been allowed to get so close to the base and drive what was, at the time, believed to be bombs into residential areas of a small village, I can’t imagine the security services allowing that to happen. “I would have expected them to have done a hard stop on the van before they got to people’s homes. So that that doesn’t feel right. “It seems insane that this appears to have been a tipoff from a member of the public, and the security services are claiming that there was a level of intelligence involved as well. I don’t see how those two things can both come through at the same time.” He went on: “Back in July, the Iranians issued a statement saying that any countries that were providing military and practical support for the American effort were legitimate targets and at the time they named RAF Fairford specifically. “So at that time, I and other civic leaders were calling for a more visible police presence to reassure residents, and that did happen. “So from July, if you were around the base, you would have seen more police patrols. “So if you’d parked a car up in a layby or somewhere near the base in the last few weeks, then you probably would have had the police contacting someone quickly to find out who you are and what you are doing. “But I do think there’s been an increase in police presence in the last week as well. So I went past the base last Monday and I noticed that the non-manned entrances to the base have been fortified with vehicles. “They put diggers and heavy vehicles in place that I’ve never seen before. So that’s quite an unusual step to block an emergency exit. So that led to speculation that maybe there was an increased level of concern from the base for them to use those measures. “I wouldn’t expect the RAF to give a running commentary,” he added. “However, I think there’s always room for improvement. We have a significant military presence surrounded on three sides by residential housing. You can walk right up to the perimeter fence. There’s lots of military bases around the world that are quite remote for good reasons. So, the reality is this is a big military presence in a rural community. “I will be asking for us to look at ways at how we can improve ongoing relations, and it’s not just relating to security matters. You know, we have other issues that you know with regard to flooding and noise, so there’s always more we can do.” Explore more on these topics UK news news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

http://www.bignewsnetwork.com/news/27930.text: Big News Network.com NATO vows more support for Ukraine after Russian drone strike WARSAW, Poland: NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said on September 14 that Russian drone strikes near the Ukraine-Poland border would lead the military alliance to increase its support for Kyiv. He described the attacks as a sign that Russian forces were becoming increasingly desperate. "The strikes yesterday on trains in Ukraine close to NATO territory again show Putin's desperation and also his desire to sow fear and terror," Rutte said at NATO headquarters in Brussels. Rutte said NATO would increase its support for Ukraine and strengthen the defenses of its 32 member countries along the alliance's eastern border with Russia. He also said Russian President Vladimir Putin would not succeed in weakening NATO's unity or stopping its support for Ukraine. Rutte's comments came after Poland announced stronger security measures along its border with Ukraine. The move followed a series of Russian drone attacks near the frontier, including two drones that came down only a few kilometers from Polish territory. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned on September 13 that Russia appeared ready to increase attacks connected to Ukraine's borders with European countries. Ukraine is already facing an intense Russian air campaign involving ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones designed to break through its air defenses. Tusk said the coming weeks and months could bring a major increase in Russian activity. He also warned that the escalation could affect Polish territory. He had issued a similar warning on September 10. Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz said on X that the Polish army had recovered what appeared to be a Russian military drone from the Baltic Sea near the coastal village of Jaroslawiec. Polish officials said intelligence assessments, including information from a CIA briefing the previous week, indicated that Russia could target border areas and increase sabotage operations in European countries. The reported aim would be to discourage Western countries from continuing their support for Ukraine. Tusk said Poland would discuss preparations for a possible joint response with its NATO allies. Polish Foreign Minister Radoslaw Sikorski highlighted NATO's military strength. He said European NATO air forces, even without U.S. involvement, would be capable of destroying half of Russia's oil refineries more quickly than Ukraine could. Deputy Defense Minister Cezary Tomczyk described the latest drone attacks as a serious escalation by Russia. He said any conflict spilling into European countries could involve sabotage, a major increase in hybrid warfare or other hostile actions along NATO's borders. The developments have increased concerns among NATO members that Russia's war against Ukraine could increasingly affect neighboring European countries. Poland, which shares a border with Ukraine and lies on NATO's eastern flank, has been particularly alert to the risk of Russian attacks or other hostile activity crossing into its territory. https://www.foodsafetynews.com/2026/09/s.text: Sign Up for Free FSN Weekly Newsletter outbreaks Salmonella found in French pumpkin seed outbreak By Joe Whitworth Published: September 28, 2026, 12:02 am | Share Share to X Share to Bluesky Share to Facebook Share to LinkedIn Share by email Sampling of pumpkin seeds and at the processing plant has detected Salmonella, according to researchers investigating an outbreak in France. A nationwide outbreak of Salmonella Enteritidis affected 81 people from May 3 to Aug. 12. The median age of patients was 35 and 56 were female. Eight people were hospitalized and two went to the emergency department because of their symptoms. On 30 July, the National Reference Centre for E. coli, Shigella and Salmonella at Institut Pasteur and Santé publique France noted an increase in a genomic cluster of Salmonella Enteritidis, with 49 isolates since May. A study in the journal Eurosurveillance reported that sick people were mainly female, with a median age of 32 and 17 were from a single region. The delay from strain isolation at the primary laboratory and sequencing results is about four weeks. Breakthrough thanks to Austria Santé publique France conducted epidemiological investigations by phone with cases, using a trawling Salmonella questionnaire of 25 pages asking about food and environmental exposures. Hypothesis generating interviews revealed most cases shopped at the Grand Frais supermarket. However, no specific food item was identified. As investigations continued, an unusually large proportion reported consuming different nuts and seeds. Pumpkin seeds have a long shelf life, are often consumed raw, and are included in snack mixes, which complicates epidemiological and traceback investigations. In August, a message was posted on EpiPulse, an online platform for European health authorities to exchange information on outbreaks. Austria reported a food isolate obtained in June from pumpkin seeds imported from Poland with an identical profile as the reference French isolate. Consumption of pumpkin seeds alone or in mixes was later confirmed for 21 of 24 patients. Traceback investigations identified one producer of pumpkin seeds that supplied Grand Frais. This firm supplied the seeds in large bags labeled with a lot number to two French contractors, who repackaged them into smaller containers for sale in bulk, or pre-packaged them ready-to-buy alone or in mixes for the supermarket. Positive samples and wider picture Samples of pumpkin seeds from Grand Frais in the original packaging were taken at the homes of three cases. All three tested positive for Salmonella Enteritidis and sequencing confirmed clustering with cases. In late August, the supplier recalled and withdrew pumpkin seed batches on the market since March. Onsite inspections identified two surface samples from the processing plant were positive for Salmonella Enteritidis, with sequencing underway. The implicated seeds were grown from seedlings imported from Austria, cultivated and processed in France. Traceback work has not been able to identify a link between the producer and pumpkin seeds from Poland. Export was identified to Belgium, Switzerland and Luxembourg through the Rapid Alert System for Food and Feed (RASFF). Switzerland and Belgium did not have any related cases but Luxembourg recorded a related human isolate on Sept. 3. This person was ill in late August and had consumed mixed nuts and raisins containing pumpkin seeds. Sampling of leftover products confirmed contamination by the outbreak strain. The United Kingdom and Portugal also reported isolates in the outbreak cluster. The UK patient had traveled to France from mid-July to early August and had symptom onset the week after return to the UK but there is no information about pumpkin seed consumption. The isolate from Portugal is from May 2026 but there is no information about a link with France or pumpkin seeds.
